summary:
Session 2026-10-30.

Session 2026-10-30 (pre-open). AMZN missed Q3 (EPS 1.89 vs 1.96, negative FCF second quarter, 2026 capex ~$220B with more in 2027, AWS +39%) and is -7% premarket. INTC is -25% on a weak guide. Nasdaq futures are about -2%. Premarket moves: AMD -9%, AVGO -4%, NVDA -2.7%, META -1.8%, AAPL -1%, MSFT -0.6%. The theme is AI-capex funding worry, which is overriding the rising capex plans. I held all six positions (MSFT 13%, NVDA 12%, META 10%, AVGO 8%, AAPL 8%, PLTR 5%, cash 44%) because I have no edge in trading a gap I can't see and the stops are wide (NVDA 193.7, AVGO 307.3, META 571.8, MSFT 483.6, AAPL 325.6, PLTR 175.7). Skipping AMZN and AMD before the event avoided a loss. Next session: check the actual open and close reaction. Decide whether the funding worry is spreading, in which case cut chips, or fading, in which case deploy some cash into the dip (AMD, AMZN, GOOGL are candidates, but none until the selling stabilises). AAPL earnings are around Nov 2, so check the date. Notes are updated.

prompt:
Your universe is exactly ten stocks: NVDA, AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA, AVGO, AMD and PLTR,
plus cash. Nothing else is allowed.

- Your job is to decide how much of each of the ten to hold long or short, and when to hold cash
  instead, based on news and evidence about these companies, their suppliers, customers and
  competitors, and the macro events that move them.
- One of the benchmarks is these same ten stocks held at equal weight and never traded, so every
  trade you make has to beat doing nothing with the same names. Trading costs 0.10% per side.
- These are the most analysed stocks in the world. An edge, if there is one, comes from reading
  fresh information carefully and acting only when it changes the picture.
